description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
Harden the pull request scan action before first use

A security audit of the action as merged found two ways a pull request
from a branch of the repository could run with the cloud credential, a
way to take a known finding out of the gate's sight, and a set of
smaller gaps between what the documentation claimed and what the code
did. This change closes what can be closed in code and documentation;
the setup script's part (environment protection, the provider
condition, the role) is a separate change, and the two are independent.

The action's steps ran in the composite default working directory, the
checkout, and `python -m pip` puts the working directory first on
sys.path: a pull request with a pip/__init__.py at its root was what the
install step imported, with the workload identity credential and the
token-minting URL in the environment, before --require-hashes or any
other control existed. Both steps now run from the action's own
directory with PYTHONSAFEPATH set and `python -P`.

The auth action writes its credential configuration into the checkout,
and that file holds the URL and token the job mints identity tokens
with. It is now moved to $RUNNER_TEMP before the scan, with every client
variable repointed, and the pipeline never lists gha-creds-*.json as a
scan target even when run on a tree without the driver.

On a pull_request event GitHub runs the pull request's copy of the
workflow file, and a job that declares the environment receives its
secrets. Nothing in code binds that. The documentation now says what it
should have said: required reviewers on the environment are mandatory
for every deployment, not a suggestion for dogfooding, with what the
reviewer must read before approving. The driver also refuses an
api-base off *.googleapis.com for a vertex_ai/ model, since litellm
would send the job's bearer token there.

The gate matched known findings by exact path, and the change set kept
only the new side of a rename: renaming a file with an open HIGH took
the finding out of the gate, and the rescan was a free re-roll. The
change set now reports renames and deletions; the gate judges a finding
at a renamed path against the new path, as direct, and treats a finding
at a deleted path as a REVIEW until someone confirms the code is gone.
Type changes (a symlink that became a file) are in the change set too.

Two policies now decide the exit status instead of one. `fail-on` is
about findings: none, block, or review, as before. `fail-closed`, new
and off by default, is about whether Mantis could look: a setup failure,
a model outage, a changed file not fully scanned, a crash. Before, those
were folded into REVIEW, which was green under `fail-on: block` -- so a
pull request that could not beat the model could make its file
unscannable instead -- and red under `fail-on: review`, so a model
outage or a sibling repository's spend on the same project stopped
every merge. Now the verdict is a function of findings only, coverage
is reported beside it (complete, partial, none, with every file and
why), the shown verdict is floored to REVIEW when coverage is
incomplete so a person knows, and `fail-closed` alone decides whether
that fails the job. A setup failure is NOT_RUN: exit 3 under
fail-closed, exit 0 otherwise, never a verdict and never silent. An
operator can install the action and not be blocked when Mantis breaks;
one who wants a green check to mean "audited in full" asks for it.

Spend. The day's meter is read again before every file, not once at
the start: it lags by minutes, so runs that start inside the window all
saw the same reading and each could spend a full run budget; now each
can overspend by about one file's share. The empty-turn retry metered
cached tokens at a fixed 0.1 whatever the run's cache discount; it now
reports counts and lets the budget weigh them. `--cache-discount 1` is
passed to every scan, run budget or not.

Smaller things from the same audit. Dependency manifests and lockfiles
are no longer in the default ignore list; a requirements.txt-only pull
request was PASS with nothing audited, and `*.txt` also swallowed
CMakeLists.txt. Credential rejection inside the pipeline is decided
from the event's error code, never its message, which a model can
write. Every angle bracket and ampersand in the step summary is
encoded, so a title cannot open a heading, a link or a collapsed block.
The JSON report goes through the credential scrubber. Meter errors no
longer print the project id. The documentation's threat model is
corrected where it overstated.

Change-Id: I231054eb3fa3d21b268a1c5bcea43a72ff6a7b54
